newsitem.title: USA: Senate puts off budget vote until Friday: Lott.
newsitem.headline: Senate puts off budget vote until Friday: Lott.

text.p: The U.S. Senate has put off its planned Thursday evening vote on a balanced budget resolution until Friday, Majority Leader Trent Lott said.

The House has approved the budget resolution but minor differences with the Senate version still have to be worked out. The House was planning to adjourn Thursday night, meaning final passage of a compromise bill would be delayed until Congress returned in early June from a Memorial Day recess.

The bipartisan plan, worked out after prolonged negotiations with the White House, would bring the deficit to zero by 2002, slow the growth of federal spending and provide a net tax cut of $85 billion through 2002.

Neither the House nor the Senate has passed any amendments that significantly alter the agreement reached with the White House but the Senate still had a number of resolutions to work through on Thursday night and Friday. Lott said the vote would take place Friday.
